SECTION_A.title: FOUNDATIONS AND PRINCIPLES OF PHYSICAL AND HEALTH EDUCATION

topics.title: Principles, meaning, scope and philosophy of Physical Education (PE)
content: a. Definition, nature, scope and objectives of PE.
b. Philosophy of the Founding Fathers of PE (Hetherington, Dudley Sergent, Thomas Wood, John Dewey).
c. History and Development of PE in: i. ancient Greece (Sparta, Athens) and Rome. ii. Pre-colonial, colonial and post-colonial eras in Nigeria.
objectives: state the meaning, nature, objectives and scope of PE;
narrate the philosophy of the Founding Fathers;
trace the historical development of PE in ancient Greece, Rome and Nigeria.
trace the origin and development of the ancient Greek festivals (Isthmian, Pythian, Nemean and the Olympian).

topics.title: Philosophy, objectives and settings of Health Education
content: a. Meaning, philosophy and objectives of Health Education
b. Settings of Health Education: i. home-based, ii. school-based, iii. community based, iv. health facility-based, v. workplace-based
c. Meaning of Health Promotion
objectives: define health education;
state the philosophy and objectives of health education;
differentiate between the meanings of health promotion and health education.

SECTION_B.title: HUMAN ANATOMY AND PHYSIOLOGY IN RELATION TO PHE

topics.title: Cells, Tissues and Systems of the Human Body
content: a. Structure and functions of a typical human cell
b. Types of cell and tissue - Epithelial, connective, muscle and nerve.
c. Cell division and differentiation - mitosis, meiosis
d. Organs and systems of the human body.
objectives: Identify cell structures and their functions
identify types of cells, tissues, organs and systems in humans;
differentiate between mitosis and meiosis;
explain cell differentiation
list organs and systems in human body

topics.title: Skeletal system
content: a. Axial and appendicular skeletons and their functions
b. Bones and joints involved in movement: i. Structure and types of bone, ii. Structure and types of joint, iii. Movements at the joints
objectives: identify the structure of the human skeleton and their functions;
identify types of bone that make up the human skeleton;
differentiate types of joint using appropriate examples;
identify the different kinds of movement permitted at joints.

topics.title: Muscular System
content: a. Major muscles of the body and their functions
b. Isometric and Isotonic contractions
objectives: identify by name and location the major muscles in human;
state the functions of major muscles in human;
differentiate between isometric and isotonic contractions

topics.title: Nervous System and Sense organs
content: a. The structures and functions of the central nervous system (Brain and Spinal Cord)
b. Types of nerve - voluntary, involuntary (simple reflex action)
c. Structure and functions of the sense organs: Skin (tactile/touch), Nose (olfactory/Smell), Tongue (taste), Ear (auditory/hearing), Eye (sight)
objectives: Identify the structures of the central nervous system;
explain the functions of the central nervous system in the body;
state the types of nerve;
describe reflex action with specific examples;
describe the structure of the sense organs and their functions.

topics.title: Circulatory System
content: a. Structure and functions of the heart and vessels;
b. Composition and functions of blood
c. Types of blood circulation (Systemic and pulmonary)
objectives: draw and label the heart;
compare the specific functions of the arteries, veins and capillaries;
identify the components of blood;
state the functions of blood;
describe the systemic and pulmonary circulations;

topics.title: Respiratory System
content: a. Structure and functions of the respiratory organs - nose, trachea and lungs
b. Process of respiration - inspiration and expiration; Tissue and cellular respiration
objectives: describe the structure of the respiratory organs and state their functions;
explain the processes of inspiration and expiration;
explain cellular and tissue respiration.

topics.title: Excretory System
content: a. Structure and functions of the kidney, skin and excretory functions of lungs;
b. Formation of excretory products — urine, sweat and carbon dioxide.
objectives: identify the structure of the kidney, skin;
state the functions of the kidney, skin and excretory functions of lungs;
explain the processes of formation of urine, sweat and carbon dioxide.

topics.title: Somatotypes and Posture
content: a. Description of endomorph, mesomorph and ectomorph;
b. Relationship between body types and physical activities.
c. Definition and characteristics of correct posture;
d. Types of postural defect - flatfoot, scoliosis, kyphosis, lordosis;
e. Causes and corrective measures of postural defects.
objectives: describe the various body types;
relate body types to performance of physical activities;
define and state the characteristics of good posture.
explain the types of postural defects;
state the causes of postural defects, for example: poor habits, accident, heredity and disease;
explain the role of exercise, nutrition, good habits and medical intervention in the correction of postural defects.

SECTION_C.title: THEORY OF PRACTICE OF SPORTS AND GAMES

topics.title: Athletics (Track and Field Events)
content: a. Track Events: Short distance races/sprints (50m, 100m, 200m, 400m, hurdles and relay races), Sprints start styles, Visual and non-visual baton take-over, Flight over hurdles, Middle and long distance races, Rules, regulations and officiating.

b. Field Events: Throwing events (discus, javelin, shotput) - facilities, equipment, styles, techniques, rules, safety; Jumping events (high jump, long jump, pole vault, triple jump) - facilities, equipment, styles, techniques, rules.
objectives: name the events... identify starting styles... differentiate baton take-over... explain relay zone... explain hurdling... describe start/stride/finish... name middle/long distance events... differentiate rules...
name throwing/jumping events... identify facilities/equipment... explain styles/techniques... explain rules... discuss safety precautions.

topics.title: Ball Games - Football and Basketball
content: a. Skills in football and basketball
b. Facilities and equipment
c. Rules, regulations and officiating
objectives: describe the skills...
identify various facilities and equipment...
identify the officials... and their functions;
differentiate the rules and regulations...

topics.title: Racket Games - Table Tennis and Badminton
content: a. Skills in table tennis and badminton
b. Specification of facilities and equipment
c. Rules, regulation and officiating
objectives: describe the skills...
identify various facilities and equipment...
identify the officials... and state their functions.
differentiate the rules and regulations...

topics.title: Food
content: a. Classes, sources and importance of food nutrients.
b. Definition and composition of balanced diet.
c. Diet planning for different groups of people (children, adolescents, athletes, pregnant women and aged);
d. Food preservation, hygiene, preservation and storage.
objectives: indicate the sources and importance of the various classes of food nutrients;
define balanced diet and state its importance;
draw up and specify dietary requirements for different groups of people;
explain methods for food preparation, preservation and storage;
explain the principles of food hygiene.

topics.title: Nutrition
content: a. Definition and nutritional values of beverages.
b. Common nutritional deficiencies and their remedies
c. Importance of water in human nutrition.
objectives: define nutrition and state the nutritional values of beverages;
state the common nutritional deficiencies and their remedies;
highlight the importance of water in human nutrition.

topics.title: Drugs
content: a. Meaning and types - stimulants, narcotics, hallucinogens, sedatives, and ergogenic aids;
b. Use, misuse, and abuse;
c. Causes and prevention of drug misuse and abuse;
d. Effects of drug misuse, abuse and self-medication on the body.
objectives: define drug and state the types;
differentiate between drug misuse and abuse;
state causes and prevention of drug misuse and abuse;
explain the effects of drug misuse, abuse and self-medication on the body.

topics.title: Physical fitness
content: a. Definition of physical fitness;
b. Components of physical fitness (health related and performance/skill related)
c. Benefits of physical activity and exercise.
objectives: define physical fitness;
outline and explain components of physical fitness;
give examples of health related and performance/skill related components;
state the benefits of physical activity and exercise.

topics.title: Conditioning Programme
content: a. Aerobic programme
b. Anaerobic programme
c. Strength training programme
d. Endurance training programme
objectives: differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic programmes;
differentiate between strength and endurance training programmes.

topics.title: Recreation and leisure
content: a. Definition and importance of recreation, leisure, work and rest;
b. Types of recreational activities (Outdoor and Indoor)
c. Differences between recreational activities and competitive sports.
objectives: differentiate among recreation, leisure, work and rest;
state the importance of recreation, leisure, work and rest;
mention types of recreation and give examples of each;
differentiate between recreational activities and competitive sports;
state safety measures in recreation.

topics.title: Dance
content: a. Definition and importance of dance.
b. Traditional dances and dance steps from various parts of Nigeria.
c. Costumes for the various traditional dances in Nigeria.
objectives: define dance and state its importance;
identify traditional dances from various parts of Nigeria;
describe the dance steps for various traditional dances in Nigeria.
identify the costumes for the various traditional dances.

topics.title: First Aid
content: a. Definition of first aid
b. Aims and principles of first aid
c. Qualities of a first aider
d. First aid box and contents
e. Common injuries that require first aid (cuts, wound, sprain, strain, dislocation, fracture)
f. Special conditions that require first aid (bleeding, burn, scald, shock, poisoning)
objectives: define first aid;
state the aims and principles of first aid;
outline the qualities of a first aider;
list the contents of the first aid box and their uses;
identify types of common injuries
identify types of common conditions that require first aid.
